messages:
IncidentBot: :warning: Runtime backpressure alert (P0) - sustained high in-flight and growing queue length on eu-west-1 affecting /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. Paging oncall.

oncall-ryan: I'm in. Dashboards show global inflight per-host at ~420, p95 queue depth 380, pod restarts: 0 but CPU steal and sched delay high since 07:14 UTC.

runtime-asha: I see a correlated rise in heavy tool-calls and function-calling sequences that create long-running generator tasks. Also noticed a recent config rollout: runtime.scheduling.v2 enabled in eu-west-1 at 07:10 by deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: rollout: runtime.scheduling.v2 -> eu-west-1 @ 07:10 UTC. No other changes.

sre-marta: Hypothesis: new scheduling interacts poorly with high-variance seq lengths, letting large batches block queues. Quick mitigations suggestion:
- apply per-route max_inflight override: /v1/chat -> 120, /v1/generate -> 100
- temporarily disable function-calling and tool invocation in streaming routes (force-call -> sync fallback)
- enable request shedding for anonymous/free API keys when queue_per_host > 180
- shorten overall connection idle + queue_timeout from 25s -> 8s
- short-term increase reserved capacity for enterprise-tiers by shifting warm pool weight +20%

oncall-ryan: Good plan. Note: dropping queue_timeout will cause more 504/429s but should free stuck resources. CS, can you prep customer comms for paid customers that may see brief latency but are being prioritized?

cs-lina: On it. I'll message enterprise contacts and offer a temporary quota bump for impacted customers. Listing known apps now.

runtime-asha: I'll apply per-route max_inflight overrides and turn off function-calling on streaming endpoints. oncall-ryan, can you flip the shedding rule?

oncall-ryan: Applying changes.

```
# ops pseudo commands
config set route.v1.chat.max_inflight 120 --region eu-west-1
config set route.v1.generate.max_inflight 100 --region eu-west-1
feature toggle function-calling --off --route /v1/chat/stream --region eu-west-1
config set runtime.queue_timeout 8s --region eu-west-1
config set runtime.shedding.anonymous_threshold 180 --region eu-west-1
route adjust warm_pool enterprise_pool +20% --region eu-west-1
```

ops-bot: Applied config changes: route overrides and queue_timeout updated. function-calling disabled on /v1/chat/stream in eu-west-1.

sre-marta: Observability update (2m after changes): inflight per-host down to ~140, queue depth p95 -> 60, error rate dropped from 14% -> 3.5%. CPU sched delay decreasing. However, some paid customers report truncated streaming responses (expected due to feature toggle).

pm-terry: We should be careful with disabling function-calling for paid users long-term. Prefer per-tenant opt-out later. For now ok as emergency mitigation.

runtime-asha: I'm also enabling short-lived aggressive request timeouts for legacy client versions that still use streaming API; command below.

```
config set client.legacy.timeout_override 6s --filter client_version<=\"1.3.2\" --region eu-west-1
```

oncall-ryan: Note: we introduced a small ingress rate-limit bump for enterprise keys to the warm pool to ensure they get priority. That should reduce impact on paying customers. Monitoring shows their p95 latency stable.

cs-lina: Notifying affected customers: "We've applied emergency traffic shaping in eu-west-1 to stabilize the service. You may see short interruptions to streaming and stricter timeouts for legacy clients. We're prioritizing enterprise traffic and will update you when streaming is restored."

sre-marta: After 10m, metrics look stable: global error rate ~1.2%, p95 latency back to ~700ms. We can keep mitigations for 30m and then start a cautious rollback: first re-enable function-calling for paid keys only, then increase per-route max_inflight in +20 increments while observing queue depth.

runtime-asha: Agreed. Also logging an action: revert runtime.scheduling.v2 in canary to validate scheduling interaction. We'll coordinate a canary tomorrow low-traffic window.

oncall-ryan: Handoff to night oncall in 25m. Summary for handoff message:
- incident: backpressure in eu-west-1 caused by scheduling rollout + heavy tool-call workloads; streaming stalled and queue grew
- mitigations: per-route max_inflight set (chat=120, generate=100), function-calling disabled for streaming in region (forced sync fallback), anonymous/free shedding when queue>180, queue_timeout shortened to 8s, enterprise warm-pool weight increased
- customer impact: free/anonymous keys may receive 429s/shorter timeouts; some paid customers saw truncated streams but were prioritized
- monitor: p95 queue depth, error rate, function-calling telemetry, per-tenant 429s
- owners: runtime-asha (canary rollback & root cause), sre-marta (monitoring & routing), cs-lina (customer comms)

pm-terry: I'll post an initial status page update and follow up with a brief post-incident note after RCA.

IncidentBot: Incident annotated. Duration so far 00:18:41. Follow-up ticket INF-4479 created for scheduling rollout RCA and per-route backpressure controls.

oncall-ryan: handing off to @oncall-jules. Leaving shedding and queue_timeout in place; please proceed with staged rollback only if queue depth <50 for 10 consecutive minutes.

oncall-jules: Copy that. Will watch dashboards and coordinate with runtime-asha for any controlled rollbacks.

cs-lina: Customers updated; two accepted temporary quota increases. Closing their tickets after 1h of stable service.

sre-marta: Good work team. Add action item: implement per-route token-aware inflight limits and better isolation for tool-calling workloads. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
